As Americans head to the polls, Republicans face a challenge that goes beyond the familiar electoral backlash against an incumbent president. For Heye, Donald Trump's greatest political vulnerability may lie in the widening gap between his rhetoric of economic success and voters' everyday financial anxieties. "For a lot of voters, they see him focused on what's important to him, not what's important to them," Heye explains. Crowds gathered in Hull city centre to welcome him, before he walked home to to his mother. British adventurer Karl Bushby has completed his 31,000-mile (50,000 km) journey from South America to Hull in the UK, reuniting with his mother at the family home 28 years after setting off. Jos Leijdekkers has been found guilty in absentia of cocaine smuggling and is believed to be in Sierra Leone. Dutch authorities have offered a record award of €2m (£1.7m/$2.24m) for information leading to the arrest of Jos Leijdekkers, one of Europe's most-wanted men. The 35-year-old, who is also known as Bolle Jos (Chubby Jos), was previously accused of being "one of the key players in international cocaine trafficking" by Dutch police. Commenting on the decision to increase the reward ten-fold, Dutch justice minister David van Weel said it was "necessary given the threat that Leijdekkers poses to national security, our democratic rule of law, and the international legal order".

Dozens of shops across European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their fridges. Supermarkets across Europe have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their fridges and freezers, and raising concern about the vulnerabilities of internet-connected hardware from industrial machinery to humble domestic appliances. Smart devices which are connected to the internet can include fridges, central heating, and even washing machines. And while that makes them easier to control remotely, in theory, any device which goes online can potentially be exploited by malicious actors.

Your fantasy football league might have its trade deadline coming up. Who should you trade for to get ready for the playoffs? Researchers have detected signals from the smallest distances ever probed. Scientists have picked up signals from the smallest scale of nature ever explored – 100 billion times smaller than an atom. The research, led by scientists based in Cambridge, was obtained from an experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). This vast machine at the European Laboratory for Particle Physics (Cern) on the Swiss-French border smashes atoms together to break them apart and discover what is inside them. The result is important because it could help researchers develop a new, more complete theory of how the Universe works.

The home secretary says the full cost of dropping plans to extend the wait for settlement will be laid out in future. A law to end surprise medical bills has generated millions of high-dollar payouts for doctors. Health plans are now fighting back by frequently withholding money. Over the past two years, Flight for Life has airlifted car crash victims, premature babies and adults struggling to breathe to hospitals across southeastern Wisconsin. Anthem, the major health insurer, covered dozens of those patients, but it has refused to pay $2.1 million it owes the company for their helicopter rides. PITTSBURGH — A lot of people like to talk about NFL teams having an identity. Saying that a team has […] Saying that a team has an identity (or needs an identity) is probably the most surface-level analysis that someone can deliver about a team. Most of the time, it doesn't mean very much, other than that the team is good at something (or isn't really good at anything). The 1972 Miami Dolphins celebrated this weekend after the previously-undefeated Vikings lost, but one member of the historic team passed away. According to an obituary published on Legacy, former Dolphins defensive lineman Bob Heinz died on Saturday at 79 years old. Heinz played collegiately at Delta College and the University of the Pacific before the Dolphins took him in the second round (No. 37 overall) of the 1969 NFL Draft. He spent nine seasons with Miami, appearing in 111 games and recording nine sacks. With Heinz on the roster, the Dolphins won two Super Bowls, including in 1972 when Miami became the first and only team to ever finish a full season without a loss on their record.
